record.title: Estonia prohibits non-exempt foreign entry during the first pandemic wave
record.scope: Admission prohibition at land/rail frontiers, alongside other modes excluded from this record
record.crossings: Estonia–Latvia and Estonia–Russia land frontiers; Ikla–Ainaži observed at partial reopening
record.movement: Foreign entrants outside permitted categories; ordinary tourism affected
record.exceptions: Citizens/residents, authorised close family, diplomatic/military personnel, goods, essential services and immediate return transit; departure not prohibited.
record.imposing_authority: Estonian Government; Police and Border Guard Board
record.enforcement: Binding admission order; Reuters observed cars passing at the Latvia frontier after midnight on 15 May.
record.consequences: Ordinary cross-border personal movement restricted; no quantified causal estimate.
record.relationship: Separate imposing authority and movement category from neighbouring-country restrictions. Reciprocal policies must not be added as extra border-wide days.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
record.official_rationale: Limit imported infection and the risk of mass COVID-19 transmission.
record.context: Emergency admission controls preceded the Baltic travel agreement; wider European-origin permission followed in June.
record.uncertainty: 15 May restored Baltic citizen/resident movement only, not all foreign entry or the Russian frontier. Earlier exceptions changed. A later government notice says 16 March retrospectively, but the original order explicitly takes effect on 17 March and controls the onset coding.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No claim of a continuous nationwide operational closure.
